cells.tense: You are taking in the whole shape of it, and it keeps getting truer.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Stay beside someone who shows you something still forming — no repairs, no ruling, your footing held while theirs wobbles.
cells.core:
You can hold the whole shape of what's growing here without sealing it shut. What you take in keeps deepening, and that's what something small needs from whoever is watching it — patience with the picture staying open. The care is steady, and it's working.

What feeds this next is a particular kind of closeness. Let someone bring you a thing they haven't solved and be in it alongside them, without tidying it or passing a verdict. Keep your own ground while you do. If they want your read, they'll ask for it, and then you give it. Neither of you has to disappear into the other.
cells.sheetLine: You see it whole, and you let it stay unfinished.

cells.tense: You will have settled what this is worth before it finishes arriving.
cells.act: choose this, not that, and mean it
cells.ask: Name one feature of something growing that's genuinely alive, just that, before you hand down a verdict on the rest — and mean your voice.
cells.core:
The read has outrun the thing it's reading. You've got the whole arc of where this goes, and the arc has gone hard into a ruling. What you call tending lands as a standard nobody asked for, and the ones who used to bring you fragile things have stopped. The verdict is doing the work, and the verdict is early.

Bring it back by holding one judgement instead of all of them. Choose a single thing here that's genuinely growing, aim your attention there, and back it with your voice. The rest can wait where it sits. Direction drawn from what's actually around you, not from what you've predicted. That alone loosens it.

cells.tense: You stood at the door long enough that the door became the subject.
cells.act: open the thing you have been assuming you knew and look at it unlabelled
cells.ask: Set down for a week the measure you're sure you've got on something here, and look at it as though you'd just met it — nothing decided, no outcome sketched.
cells.core:
Something close by has been waiting on your attention, and you've stayed at the edge of it — circling, reading around it, not landing. What's pointed at the idea of the thing rather than the thing itself. Nothing in the pot has been brought along, and that bringing-along is what's missing.

What starts it is beginning again on a small piece. Take something you assume you know and look at it with the name peeled off. Meet it with nothing decided, no outcome sketched. You don't have to know what it becomes — you can't, and that's alright. Being here with it, open, is the first move, and it's enough to restart the caring.

cells.tense: Your hand is steadying the shares here, and you say it's just how things go.
cells.act: adjust the share until it is fair, then stop
cells.ask: Catch your own hand while it evens out who gives what here — make the change, then leave it and don't recheck.
cells.core:
On its good days this looks easy: one person gets what they need, another takes less without being asked, and nobody's counting. An exchange moving both ways, unwatched. That's the shape of it when it's working, and you're what keeps it moving. Asked about it, you'd say the shares just sort themselves out.

So catch the hand as it moves. When you nudge who gets what, or quietly take less yourself, recognize that it's your doing — then do it and stop. No revisiting it, no tally. The one holding a balance and a bystander look the same from outside; the only difference is that one of them knows.
